text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Tuesday.

GERMANY - German bunds, futures closed weaker as mark gained on dollar, while worries grow about chances of Germany qualifying for European monetary union. The June Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 100.03, down 0.38 from Monday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - Gilts closed lower in a session of thin futures volumes with trade in Bunds dominating, dealers said. The June long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 110-05/32, down 07/32 from Monday's settlement price.

FRANCE - June bond futures settled lower after volatile session. EMU jitters continue to unnerve but non-residents largely absent after heavy selling on Monday. The June notional bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 127.92 down 0.40 from Monday's settlement price.

ITALY - Italian debt markets came under another day of pressure as the lira lost ground on the mark amid continuing concerns about prospects for European monetary union. The June bond future on LIFFE was trading at 124.12 down 0.23 from Monday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - US Treasuries were steady to a touch lower in late morning trade after earlier short-covering and hedge fund buying, traders say dealers now setting up new shorts ahead of CPI on Wednesday. The June Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 108 21/32, down 03/32 from Monday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 6.96 percent.

JAPAN - The key June Japanese government bond futures contract fell sharply on Tuesday due to comments by a senior Bank of Japan official which seemed to imply that the recent surge in JGBs had been overdone, traders said. In after hours trading the June future on LIFFE was trading at 125.92, down 0.51 from Monday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

EUROBONDS - The highlight of a quiet primary market on Tuesday was the launch of the first euro-denominated Eurobond for a sovereign, namely Italy's 1.0 billion euro seven-year Eurobond. WestMerchant announced it had won the mandate to lead manage a debut Eurobond for Russia's region of Sverdlovsk. Brazil's media company RBS Participacoes set a $125 million 10-year bond.
